Endocrinology · published research

Pancreatic duct regeneration

One small randomized rat study found more pancreatic duct and islet regeneration, higher liver and muscle glycogen, and improved insulin-tolerance testing after near-infrared LED treatment. Human evidence is absent.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One small randomized rat study found more pancreatic duct and islet regeneration, higher liver and muscle glycogen, and improved insulin-tolerance testing after near-infrared LED treatment. Human evidence is absent.

Summary of the Evidence

One exact-category publication reports a randomized preclinical study in 20 Wistar rats with streptozotocin-induced diabetes. The animals were divided among three groups, including PBM-treated and untreated diabetic groups. No duplicate report or independent replication in this category is identified. The experiment tests tissue and metabolic outcomes in one chemically induced diabetes model.

Human and clinical evidence

No human study directly examining pancreatic duct regeneration after PBM was identified. The rat findings do not establish that the same tissue response occurs in people.

Animal evidence

The study applied LED treatment over the pancreatic projection for five consecutive days and evaluated the animals 30 days later. Histological assessments showed increased pancreatic islet and duct regeneration in treated diabetic rats. The treated group also had a different insulin-tolerance test result and higher liver and skeletal-muscle glycogen than untreated diabetic controls. These outcomes indicate changes in tissue appearance and glucose-related metabolism in the tested model (Tatmatsu-Rocha et al. 2017).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No exact-category cell-culture or ex-vivo study of pancreatic duct regeneration was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The rat experiment used 805-nm near-infrared LED light at 40 mW, with 0.88 J delivered per spot over an area of 0.196 cm², equivalent to about 4.49 J/cm² per spot. Each session lasted 22 seconds and was repeated on five consecutive days over the pancreas. This single protocol was not compared with another wavelength or dose, and external treatment over a rat abdomen does not establish how much light would reach a human pancreas.

Interpretation

The study reports favorable histological and metabolic differences in treated rats, including more duct and islet regeneration and higher glycogen measures. The findings merit independent testing, but one small animal experiment cannot establish durable endocrine recovery or show that ductal changes produced functional beta cells. Human benefit remains untested.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for pancreatic duct and islet regeneration in rats
Publications and records1 article

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One randomized experiment in diabetic rats reported increased duct and islet regeneration, higher glycogen measures, and a difference in insulin-tolerance testing after PBM. These are favorable animal findings, but the study has not been independently replicated and does not show a durable human effect. Replication with blinded tissue analysis and sustained metabolic follow-up would support a stronger conclusion.
